questions.stem: Which component is considered the 'brain' of the computer, performing arithmetic and logical operations?
questions.explanation: The CPU (Central Processing Unit), often called the 'brain' of the computer, executes instructions and performs arithmetic/logical operations. It has two main units: the ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) and the CU (Control Unit). RAM is temporary memory, the hard disk is permanent storage, and the motherboard is the main circuit board connecting all components.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an input device?
questions.explanation: A keyboard is an input device — it sends data into the computer. A monitor, printer, and speaker are all output devices, which display or produce information from the computer. Other common input devices include the mouse, scanner, microphone, and webcam.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which type of memory is volatile, meaning its contents are lost when the computer is switched off?
questions.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) is volatile — it temporarily holds data and programs currently in use, and its contents are erased when power is lost. ROM (Read-Only Memory) is non-volatile and retains data permanently. Hard disks and flash drives are non-volatile secondary storage.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: The full form of 'CPU' is:
questions.explanation: CPU stands for Central Processing Unit. It is the primary component that carries out the instructions of a computer program by performing basic arithmetic, logic, controlling, and input/output operations. Modern CPUs are housed on a single chip called a microprocessor.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which of these is a pointing (input) device?
questions.explanation: A mouse is a pointing input device used to control the cursor on screen. A plotter and projector are output devices (a plotter prints vector graphics; a projector displays images), and a monitor is the primary display output device. Other pointing devices include the trackball, touchpad, and joystick.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: The two main components of the CPU are the Control Unit and the:
questions.explanation: The CPU has two principal components: the Control Unit (CU), which directs and coordinates operations, and the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), which performs all arithmetic (add, subtract) and logical (compare, AND/OR) operations. Registers provide fast temporary storage within the CPU.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which unit of memory is the smallest?
questions.explanation: A bit (binary digit, 0 or 1) is the smallest unit of computer memory. The ascending order is: bit → nibble (4 bits) → byte (8 bits) → kilobyte (1024 bytes) → megabyte → gigabyte → terabyte. A nibble is half a byte.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: How many bytes are there in one kilobyte (KB) in the traditional binary definition?
questions.explanation: In the traditional binary definition used in computing, 1 kilobyte (KB) = 1024 bytes (2^10). The progression is 1 KB = 1024 B, 1 MB = 1024 KB, 1 GB = 1024 MB, 1 TB = 1024 GB. (The decimal SI definition uses 1000, but exams typically expect 1024 for KB.)
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which of the following is both an input and an output device?
questions.explanation: A touchscreen is both an input and output device: it displays information (output) and accepts touch commands (input). Other I/O devices include modems, network cards, and headsets (with mic). A scanner, light pen, and barcode reader are input-only devices.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: The main circuit board of a computer that holds the CPU, memory, and connectors is called the:
questions.explanation: The motherboard (also called the mainboard or system board) is the primary printed circuit board that houses the CPU, RAM slots, expansion slots, and connectors, allowing all components to communicate. The chipset on the motherboard manages data flow between the processor, memory, and peripherals.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which type of memory is non-volatile and stores the BIOS / firmware used to boot the computer?
questions.explanation: ROM (Read-Only Memory) is non-volatile and stores the BIOS/firmware (the startup instructions) needed to boot the computer. Its contents are retained without power. RAM and cache are volatile working memory; registers are tiny ultra-fast storage inside the CPU. Variants of ROM include PROM, EPROM, and EEPROM.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the fastest type of memory in a computer, located closest to the CPU?
questions.explanation: Registers (inside the CPU) and cache memory are the fastest memory, located closest to the processor. The memory hierarchy from fastest/smallest to slowest/largest is: Registers → Cache (L1, L2, L3) → Main RAM → Secondary storage (SSD/HDD) → Tertiary (optical/tape). Speed decreases and capacity increases as you move away from the CPU.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which storage device uses flash memory and has no moving parts, offering faster access than a traditional hard disk?
questions.explanation: An SSD (Solid State Drive) uses flash memory with no moving mechanical parts, making it faster, quieter, and more durable than a traditional HDD (which uses spinning magnetic platters and a read/write head). SSDs have largely replaced HDDs in modern laptops for performance.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which port is most commonly used today to connect peripherals like keyboards, mice, and pen drives?
questions.explanation: USB (Universal Serial Bus) is the most common port for connecting peripherals like keyboards, mice, pen drives, and printers. It supports plug-and-play and hot-swapping. The older PS/2 (keyboard/mouse), parallel (LPT, for old printers), and serial (COM) ports have largely been replaced by USB.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: What does GPU stand for, the component specialised for rendering graphics?
questions.explanation: GPU stands for Graphics Processing Unit, a specialised processor designed to render images, video, and animations efficiently through parallel processing. GPUs are also widely used today for AI/machine learning and cryptocurrency mining due to their parallel computing power. They may be integrated or dedicated (discrete).
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Arrange these memory units in ascending order of size: Terabyte, Megabyte, Gigabyte, Kilobyte.
questions.explanation: Ascending order: Kilobyte (KB) < Megabyte (MB) < Gigabyte (GB) < Terabyte (TB). Each is 1024 times the previous (binary). Beyond TB come Petabyte (PB), Exabyte (EB), Zettabyte (ZB), and Yottabyte (YB).
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which device converts digital signals to analog and vice versa, enabling internet connectivity over telephone lines?
questions.explanation: A modem (modulator-demodulator) converts digital signals from a computer into analog signals for transmission over telephone/cable lines (modulation) and back (demodulation). A router directs data between networks; a switch connects devices within a LAN; a hub is a simpler, less intelligent connector.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an output device?
questions.explanation: A plotter is an output device that draws vector graphics/large-format prints (used in engineering and architecture). A joystick, optical mark reader (OMR), and webcam are all input devices. Common output devices include the monitor, printer, plotter, speakers, and projector.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Cache memory is used to:

options.text: Provide backup storage for the hard disk
Store frequently accessed data for faster CPU access
Connect the computer to a network

questions.explanation: Cache memory is a small, very fast memory between the CPU and main RAM that stores frequently accessed data and instructions, reducing the average time to access memory. It comes in levels (L1 fastest/smallest, L2, L3 larger/slower). This bridges the speed gap between the fast CPU and slower RAM.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which generation of computers introduced the use of integrated circuits (ICs)?
questions.explanation: The third generation of computers (1965–1971) introduced integrated circuits (ICs), which replaced transistors and dramatically reduced size and cost. The generations are: 1st — vacuum tubes; 2nd — transistors; 3rd — integrated circuits; 4th — microprocessors (VLSI); 5th — artificial intelligence (ongoing).
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: A student claims 'ROM is faster than RAM because it is permanent.' Which assessment is correct?

options.text: Incorrect — RAM is faster than ROM; volatility is unrelated to speed, and RAM is the working memory the CPU actively reads/writes during operation
Correct — non-volatile memory is always faster
Correct — ROM has direct CPU access while RAM does not
Incorrect — both have identical speed since both are primary memory

questions.explanation: The claim is INCORRECT. RAM is faster than ROM. Volatility (whether memory is retained without power) is independent of speed. RAM is the active working memory that the CPU reads from and writes to during program execution, and it is optimised for speed. ROM is read-mostly, stores firmware, and is slower. Permanence does not imply speed.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which statement about the difference between a compiler and an interpreter (in the context of how hardware executes code) is correct?

options.text: A compiler executes line by line; an interpreter translates everything first
A compiler translates the entire program into machine code at once before execution; an interpreter translates and executes line by line
Both translate the whole program before any execution
Neither produces machine code; both run on the GPU directly

questions.explanation: A compiler translates the entire source program into machine code in one pass, producing an executable that the hardware runs directly (faster execution, e.g. C/C++). An interpreter translates and executes the program statement by statement at runtime (easier debugging, e.g. Python in interpreted mode). This is a frequently-tested distinction.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'firmware' stored in a computer is best described as:

options.text: Application software installed by the user
Temporary data held in RAM during execution
Software permanently programmed into hardware (e.g., BIOS in ROM) to control low-level functions
Documents stored on the hard disk

questions.explanation: Firmware is specialised software permanently (or semi-permanently) programmed into hardware, typically stored in ROM/flash, that controls the device's low-level functions — for example, the BIOS/UEFI that initialises hardware at startup. It sits between pure hardware and higher-level software, and is updated rarely (a 'firmware update').
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the function of the system bus in a computer?

options.text: It cools the CPU to prevent overheating
It supplies electrical power to all components
It stores the operating system permanently
It is the pathway that carries data, addresses, and control signals between the CPU, memory, and I/O devices

questions.explanation: The system bus is the communication pathway that transfers data between the CPU, memory, and I/O devices. It comprises three parts: the data bus (carries actual data), the address bus (carries memory addresses), and the control bus (carries control/timing signals). Bus width affects how much data can be transferred at once.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: What is the primary advantage of a 64-bit processor over a 32-bit processor?

options.text: It consumes exactly half the power
It is physically smaller in size
It can address far more memory (RAM) — well beyond the ~4 GB limit of 32-bit systems — and process more data per cycle
It does not require an operating system

questions.explanation: A 64-bit processor can address vastly more memory than a 32-bit one. A 32-bit system can address only about 4 GB of RAM (2^32 bytes), whereas a 64-bit system can theoretically address 2^64 bytes (about 16 exabytes), and practically supports very large RAM. It also handles larger chunks of data per operation, improving performance for demanding applications.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
